message:
The repo is at 2018-09-13. So the OSS-Fuzz issue 42470383 is from around this time. Let me look at the format 4 `collect_unicodes` in this version. The `glyphIdArrayLength` off-by-one is present.

Let me reconsider the READ 4. The issue says "heap-buffer-overflow READ 4". Let me reconsider whether the format 4 `collect_unicodes` can cause a READ 4.

Actually, let me reconsider. The `glyphIdArrayLength` off-by-one allows reading `glyphIdArray[glyphIdArrayLength - 1]` at byte offset `length`. But this is a 2-byte read (HBUINT16).

Wait, but maybe the READ 4 is in the format 12/13. Let me reconsider. Actually, let me reconsider whether the format 12/13 `collect_unicodes` can be triggered with an out-of-bounds `groups[i]` read.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. Let me look at the format 4 `collect_unicodes` once more and think about whether the `glyphIdArray[index]` read can be a 4-byte read.

Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the READ 4 is in the format 4 `collect_unicodes` reading `this->startCount[i]` where `i` can be out of bounds. Let me reconsider the loop:

```cpp
unsigned int count = this->segCount;
if (count && this->startCount[count - 1] == 0xFFFFu)
  count--; /* Skip sentinel segment. */
for (unsigned int i = 0; i < count; i++)
{
  unsigned int rangeOffset = this->idRangeOffset[i];
  if (rangeOffset == 0)
    out->add_range (this->startCount[i], this->endCount[i]);
  ...
```

`count = segCount`. `startCount[count-1]` reads `startCount[segCount-1]`. `startCount` has `segCount` entries, so this is within bounds. Then `count--` makes `count = segCount - 1`. The loop reads `startCount[i]`, `endCount[i]`, `idRangeOffset[i]` for `i < segCount-1`, all within bounds.

Hmm. So format 4 seems safe except for the off-by-one in glyphIdArrayLength.

Let me reconsider. Maybe the READ 4 is in the format 12/13 and the sanitize is bypassed because the `groups` array's `len` is validated against the blob, but the `collect_unicodes` reads `groups[i]` where `i` can be `groups.len` (one past the end) due to some off-by-one.

Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the issue is that the format 12/13 `collect_unicodes` reads `groups[i].startCharCode` and `groups[i].endCharCode`, both HBUINT32 (4 bytes). If `groups.len` is validated to be within the blob, then reading `groups[i]` for `i < groups.len` is within bounds. So no overflow.

Hmm. Let me reconsider. Maybe the READ 4 is in the format 4 `collect_unicodes` reading `this->glyphIdArray[index]` where `index` can be large, and the READ is 4 bytes because... no, glyphIdArray is HBUINT16.
